body:
## Problem

The "open or update PR" step creates a PR only when `gh pr view sync/formulae` fails. For a branch argument, gh resolves PRs in any state, so once one sync PR has been merged the check always succeeds and `gh pr create` never runs again.

## Evidence

sync-formulae.yml:77: `if ! gh pr view sync/formulae >/dev/null 2>&1; then gh pr create ...`

Observed 2026-10-16 with gh 2.102.0:
- `gh pr list --head sync/formulae --state all` -> `68 MERGED created=2026-07-29 merged=2026-07-30`
- `gh pr view sync/formulae --json number,state` -> `68 MERGED`, exit 0

No sync PR has been opened since #68. The four most recent daily runs logged "No formula changes", so the defect has not fired yet.

## Impact

On the next upstream release, the job commits the regenerated formulae, force-pushes sync/formulae, sees PR #68 and exits green. No PR is created, so the formula update never reaches main and nothing signals it: the run is "success". Each later run repeats this.

## Fix

Check for an open PR specifically:

```bash
if [ -z "$(gh pr list --head sync/formulae --state open --json number --jq '.[0].number')" ]; then
  gh pr create ...
fi
```

`gh pr list` defaults to open PRs; `--state open` makes it explicit.

## Resolution
sync-formulae.yml checks for an open PR with `gh pr list --head sync/formulae --state open`; merged/closed PRs no longer suppress gh pr create.
title: Sync job never opens a PR again: gh pr view matches the merged sync PR

body:
## Problem

The delegated click handler finds its target with the selector `input[readonly][onclick*="select"]`, then immediately calls `input.removeAttribute("onclick")`. After the first click the input no longer matches the selector, so every later click on it does nothing: no copy, no "Copied!" feedback.

## Evidence

main.js:109: `const input = e.target.closest('input[readonly][onclick*="select"]');`
main.js:111: `input.removeAttribute("onclick");`

The inputs come from _command_input.html.erb:7 and formula.html.erb:97, which carry `onclick="this.select()"`. Once removed, no other selector or handler matches them.

## Impact

On every page, a second attempt to copy the same `brew` command or SHA256 silently fails. For example, a visitor copies, pastes, mistypes and copies again. The clipboard keeps whatever was there before, and since the first copy showed "Copied!", the user is likely to paste stale content.

## Fix

Match on a stable marker instead of the attribute being deleted. Mark the inputs with `data-copy` in both templates and drop the inline `onclick`, since the handler already selects the text:

```js
const input = e.target.closest("input[data-copy]");
if (input) {
  const success = await copyToClipboard(input);
  showCopyFeedback(input, success);
}
```

## Resolution
Inputs carry a stable data-copy marker; inline onclick dropped; main.js matches input[data-copy] and never removes it.
title: Click-to-copy works only on the first click of each input

body:
## Problem

Make runs each recipe line with `/bin/sh -c` (no `-e`; the Makefile sets no .SHELLFLAGS). Three patterns lose failures:
1. `test` and `check` write every probe as `cmd && echo "✅ ..." || echo "❌ ..."`, so the line exits 0 whether cmd passed or failed.
2. `build`, `serve` and `parse` run `bundle exec ruby parse_formulas.rb; bundle exec ruby build_site.rb;` inside one `if` block. The block's status is the last command's, so a parse failure is discarded when build_site succeeds.
3. `test` then prints "✅ All tests passed!" unconditionally.

## Evidence

Makefile:116: `@$(RUBY) -c $(SCRIPTS_DIR)/parse_formulas.rb && echo "✅ parse_formulas.rb syntax OK" || echo "❌ parse_formulas.rb syntax error"`. Lines 105-112 and 117-120 use the same form.
Makefile:37-38: `bundle exec $(RUBY) $(SCRIPTS_DIR)/parse_formulas.rb; \` then `bundle exec $(RUBY) $(SCRIPTS_DIR)/build_site.rb; \`

Reproduced with make's own shell (`make -p` shows `.SHELLFLAGS := -c`, `SHELL = /bin/sh`):
- `sh -c 'false && echo ok || echo "syntax error"'` prints "syntax error", status=0
- `sh -c 'if true; then false; true; fi'` -> status=0

## Impact

`make test` exits 0 with "All tests passed!" when any of five scripts has a syntax error. Only test_sync_formulae.rb on the last line can fail it. `make build`, which pages-build.yml:49 runs, publishes a site from a stale or missing formulae.json when parse_formulas.rb fails, and the deploy goes green.

## Fix

Make recipe shells fail fast, and let failures propagate:

```make
SHELL := /bin/bash
.SHELLFLAGS := -eu -o pipefail -c
```

Replace each `cmd && echo OK || echo FAIL` with plain `cmd` (or `cmd || { echo FAIL; exit 1; }` if the message matters). With `-e`, the `;`-joined parse/build lines stop at the first failure.

## Resolution
Makefile sets SHELL=/bin/bash and .SHELLFLAGS=-eu -o pipefail -c; `&& echo || echo` patterns removed. Verified: a formula without a class line makes `make build` exit 2.
title: make test, check and build report success after a failing step

body:
## Problem

The only job that runs `make build` is pages-build, and it runs on push to main, filtered to Formula/theme/four build scripts. ci.yml runs only `brew test-bot --only-tap-syntax`. No workflow runs `make build` on a pull request. No workflow runs `ruby scripts/test_sync_formulae.rb` (or `make test`) at all.

## Evidence

pages-build.yml:3-17: `on: push: branches: [main]`, with `paths:` listing only `Formula/**`, `theme/**` and four scripts. The comment explicitly keeps Gemfile.lock out.

ci.yml:36-37: the only step is `uses: ./.github/actions/ci`, which ends at `brew test-bot --only-tap-syntax` (action.yml:92).

Observed: PR #78 (json 2.21.2 -> 3.0.2) passed CI and merged as b173962. `gh run list --branch main` shows only a "Sync formulae" run for b173962, with no "Build and Deploy Documentation" run. `make build` was broken from that commit (`ArgumentError: unknown keyword: create_additions` in execjs 2.10.1) until #79 fixed it. The breakage was found by hand.

## Impact

A dependency bump or a script change can break the site build or the formula generator's tested functions and still merge green. The breakage surfaces only on the next Formula/theme push, as a failed Pages deploy. For sync_formulae.rb, its offline tests are never executed by CI.

## Fix

Add a job to ci.yml that runs on every PR (no path filter):

```yaml
  site:
    name: Build site and run tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@14594264cd68ce8a2345dd349bc3d138a4ef85c8 # v1.327.0
        with:
          bundler-cache: true
      - run: bundle exec ruby scripts/test_sync_formulae.rb
      - run: make build
```

Keep pages-build's path filter, since it only governs deploys.

## Resolution
ci.yml gains a `site` job (no path filter, contents: read) running `make test` and `make build` on every PR.
title: No PR check runs the site build or the unit tests; json 3 bump merged with a broken build

body:
## Problem

The checks named "parse_formulas regex round-trips the release date" and "version is recoverable from the asset URL" do not call parse_formulas.rb. They re-type its regexes inline, so if FormulaParser::PATTERNS or extract_version changes, these tests still pass while the real sync→parse contract breaks.

Separately, no test exists for:
- parse_formulas.rb (extract_version, extract_dependencies, PATTERNS)
- build_site.rb's group_formulae/sort_versions: version grouping, the synthesized-main path, unparseable versions → 0
- theme/main.js (fuzzyMatch, the copy handler; the latter has a confirmed bug filed separately)

## Evidence

test_sync_formulae.rb:183: comment "Homebrew and parse_formulas.rb#extract_version get it now", then line 185: `url = body[/^\s*url "([^"]+)"/, 1]` and `url.match(/v?(\d+(?:\.\d+)+)/)`, an inline copy of parse_formulas.rb:20 and :107.
test_sync_formulae.rb:193-195: "The parse_formulas regex must recover exactly what formula_body emits.", then `released = body[/^#\s*released:\s*(\S+)/, 1]`, a copy of parse_formulas.rb:25.
`rg 'FormulaParser|parse_formulas' scripts/test_sync_formulae.rb` matches only comments and the check name; there is no require.
The only test file in the repo is scripts/test_sync_formulae.rb.

## Impact

The one cross-stage contract the architecture depends on, formula file to formulae.json, is asserted against a copy of the consumer. A parser regex change that drops `released_at`, or that misreads calver versions, passes every test, and the site silently loses release dates or shows wrong versions. Version grouping on the site has no regression protection.

## Fix

- In test_sync_formulae.rb, `require_relative "parse_formulas"`, write formula_body output to a temp file, and assert on `FormulaParser.new.send(:parse_formula, path)`: `[:released_at] == "2026-03-04T12:00:00Z"` and `[:version] == "2026.03.4"`. Delete the inline regex copies.
- Add checks for SiteBuilder#group_formulae: mains get sorted `versions`, an orphan `x@1.0` synthesizes main `x`, and `"garbage"` versions sort as 0.
- Run the tests in CI (see the CI finding).

## Resolution
test_sync_formulae.rb parses formula_body output with the real FormulaParser (version, released_at, escaped desc); regex copies deleted; added SiteBuilder#group_formulae checks (sorted versions, orphan main synthesis, unparseable version sorts last). CI runs it via `make test`.
title: Stage-contract tests copy the parser's regexes; parse and build stages are untested

body:
## Problem

Every generated page loads `https://cdn.tailwindcss.com?plugins=forms,typography` at runtime. The URL is unversioned and has no `integrity` attribute. Tailwind documents this script as development-only. It downloads a JIT compiler and generates the CSS in each visitor's browser on every page load.

## Evidence

_head.html.erb:6: `<script src="https://cdn.tailwindcss.com?plugins=forms,typography"></script>`, followed by an inline `tailwind.config = { darkMode: "class" }`.

tailwindcss.com/docs/installation/play-cdn (fetched 2026-10-16): "The Play CDN is designed for development purposes only, and is not intended for production."

## Impact

Integrity: whatever that host serves runs with full DOM access on the tap's site. The site's purpose is the `brew tap` and `brew install ivuorinen/tap/<name>` commands visitors copy, and a tampered script can rewrite them to another tap. Stability: the unversioned URL tracks upstream, so a breaking change restyles the site with no commit here. Performance: every visit downloads and runs a CSS compiler and flashes unstyled content first. With JS disabled or the CDN blocked, the site is unstyled.

## Fix

Compile the CSS at build time and ship it as a static file. The official `tailwindcss-ruby` gem wraps the standalone Tailwind CLI and fits the existing Ruby build:

1. Add `gem "tailwindcss-ruby"` to the Gemfile.
2. In asset_processor.rb's generate_css, run `tailwindcss -i theme/style.css -o docs/style.css --minify --content "theme/**/*.erb,theme/main.js"`. On Tailwind v4, use `@import "tailwindcss"; @plugin "@tailwindcss/forms"; @plugin "@tailwindcss/typography";` and a `@custom-variant dark` rule in style.css instead of `--content`.
3. Delete the CDN `<script>` and the inline `tailwind.config` block from _head.html.erb.

## Resolution
CSS compiled at build time by tailwindcss-ruby 4.3.3 (Tailwind v4, forms plugin, class-based dark variant, sources limited to theme/); CDN script and inline config removed; cssminify2 dropped. v3->v4 renames applied (shadow-sm->xs, backdrop-blur->-sm, outline-none->outline-hidden, placeholder-*->placeholder:text-*). Every template class verified present in docs/style.css; not checked visually in a browser.
title: Published site loads the unpinned Tailwind Play CDN script, without SRI, on every page

body:
## Problem

build_metas removes drafts only. run() then treats index 0 of the releases list as the latest, writing the plain `name.rb` from it (`outputs_for(meta, latest: idx.zero?)`). Neither step looks at `prerelease`, or at the repo's designated latest release. The list order is creation order, not version order.

## Evidence

sync_formulae.rb:209: `releases = gh_json("repos/#{repo}/releases?per_page=100").reject { |r| r["draft"] }`
run(): `outputs_for(meta, latest: idx.zero?)`
`rg prerelease scripts .github README.md docs/plans` -> no matches.

Scenario: a repo publishes `2.0.0-rc.1` (prerelease), or publishes `1.4.2` after `2.0.0`. Either is index 0, so `brew install ivuorinen/tap/<name>` installs the rc, or downgrades from 2.0.0 to 1.4.2. None of the five source repos has a prerelease today (checked with gh api), so the defect is latent.

## Impact

Every user of the unversioned formula gets a prerelease build, or a silent downgrade, on the next `brew upgrade`. Nothing flags it: test-bot validates syntax, not which version was chosen.

## Fix

Use GitHub's own notion of latest. `GET repos/{repo}/releases/latest` excludes drafts and prereleases and honours the "Set as latest" flag:

```ruby
latest_tag = gh_json("repos/#{repo}/releases/latest")["tag_name"]
releases = gh_json("repos/#{repo}/releases?per_page=100").reject { |r| r["draft"] || r["prerelease"] }
```

Then pass `latest: meta[:tag] == latest_tag`, with build_release_meta keeping `tag: release["tag_name"]`. Add a fixture test where the first row is a prerelease.

## Resolution
build_metas uses releases/latest for the unversioned formula and drops prereleases; metas carry :tag. Test covers a leading prerelease and a backport listed first. Live `make sync` produced no formula diff.
title: Unversioned formula tracks the first API row, so prereleases and backports become "latest"

body:
## Problem

formula_body builds Ruby source by pasting values into double-quoted literals: `%Q(  desc "#{meta[:desc]}")`, and the same for homepage, license, bin, url and sha256. desc comes from the GitHub repo description via sanitize_desc, which only trims whitespace, drops articles and truncates. No value is escaped.

## Evidence

sync_formulae.rb:106: `lines << %Q(  desc "#{meta[:desc]}")`. The other unescaped sites are lines 107, 112, 119, 122, 148 and 149.

Reproduced 2026-10-16 by calling SyncFormulae.formula_body with sanitize_desc(input) and compiling the result with RubyVM::InstructionSequence.compile:
- `Make "fast" tools` -> `desc "Make "fast" tools"` -> SyntaxError
- ``Runs #{`id`} here`` -> ``desc "Runs #{`id`} here"`` -> parses: valid Ruby that runs `id` when the class body is evaluated

## Impact

A repo description containing `"` turns the daily sync red with an unloadable formula. A description containing `#{...}` produces a formula that passes `brew test-bot --only-tap-syntax` and runs arbitrary commands on every user's machine whenever brew loads it. Anyone who can edit a listed source repo's description can change that string, including admins and compromised accounts. The same applies to license (spdx_id) and to asset-derived URLs.

## Fix

Emit every value as an escaped Ruby literal with String#inspect. It escapes `"`, `\` and `#{`:

```ruby
lines << "  desc #{meta[:desc].inspect}"
lines << "  homepage #{meta[:homepage].inspect}"
lines << "  license #{meta[:license].inspect}" if meta[:license]
# ...the same for bin, url and sha256
```

Add a test_sync_formulae.rb check that formula_body output with a desc of `a "b" #{c}` compiles and that `desc` round-trips the exact text.

## Resolution
formula_body emits desc, homepage, license, bin, url, sha256 (and the default test's bin) via String#inspect. Parser QUOTED regex accepts backslash escapes and unescapes. Test: desc with quotes and #{...} parses with Prism as a plain StringNode and round-trips through FormulaParser.
title: Generated formulae interpolate GitHub API strings into Ruby literals unescaped

body:
## Problem

The License and version badges put small white text (text-xs, 12px semibold) on mid-tone fills. The sky-600 links (text-sm) are also below the AA minimum for normal text (1.4.3: 4.5:1).

## Evidence

_formula_card.html.erb:44: `bg-sky-500 ... text-white dark:bg-sky-400`. Line 47: `bg-emerald-500 ... text-white dark:bg-emerald-400`. formula.html.erb:117 uses the same emerald badge for versions.
index.html.erb:26, _formula_card.html.erb:28 and formula.html.erb:59/116 use `text-sky-600` links on the slate-50/white page background.

Computed WCAG ratios (Tailwind palette hex, relative-luminance formula):
- white on sky-500 2.77:1; white on emerald-500 2.54:1
- white on sky-400 (dark) 2.14:1; white on emerald-400 (dark) 1.92:1
- sky-600 on slate-50 3.91:1

Every one is below 4.5:1. The dep badge (white on slate-800, 14.63:1) passes.

## Impact

The license and version are hard to read for low-vision users and in bright light, especially in dark mode at 1.9-2.1:1. The links' text fails AA as well.

## Fix

Use darker fills, or dark text on light fills:
- License: `bg-sky-700 text-white` (light) and `dark:bg-sky-300 dark:text-slate-900`
- Version: `bg-emerald-700 text-white` and `dark:bg-emerald-300 dark:text-slate-900`
- Links: `text-sky-700` (light) and keep `dark:text-sky-400`

Re-check each pair at ≥ 4.5:1.

## Resolution
License badge bg-sky-700/white, dark bg-sky-300/slate-900; version badges (card and formula page) bg-emerald-700/white, dark bg-emerald-300/slate-900; links text-sky-700 (hover sky-800), dark sky-400 kept.
title: Badge and link text fail WCAG 2.2 AA contrast (1.92-3.91:1)

body:
## Problem

The build job is granted `pages: write` and `id-token: write`, each commented "required by actions/deploy-pages". The build job does not run deploy-pages: it runs `make setup` (bundle install), `make build`, configure-pages and upload-pages-artifact. Only the deploy job (lines 61-77) needs those scopes.

## Evidence

pages-build.yml:30-33 (build job):
```yaml
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pages: write # required by actions/deploy-pages to publish the Pages deployment
      id-token: write # required by actions/deploy-pages for OIDC authentication
```
pages-build.yml:47-49 runs `make setup` and `make build`, which install and execute gems (terser/execjs, cssminify2).

The actions/deploy-pages README says: "The job that executes the deployment must at minimum have the following permissions: `pages: write`, `id-token: write`". That job is `deploy` here, which already declares both.

## Impact

Any code that runs during `make setup` or `make build` can mint an OIDC token and has Pages write, for example a compromised gem release pulled by a Renovate bump. That code then holds the deployment credentials the split into build and deploy jobs exists to isolate. The comments state a false requirement, so a reader keeps the scopes.

## Fix

Reduce the build job to what its steps use:

```yaml
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pages: read # actions/configure-pages reads the Pages site config
```

Leave `pages: write` and `id-token: write` on the deploy job only.

## Resolution
pages-build build job reduced to contents: read, pages: read; pages: write and id-token: write remain on deploy only.
title: Pages build job holds id-token: write and pages: write while running third-party gem code

body:
## Problem

Several README statements are false against the current code:
1. Line 75, "custom Ruby-based static site generator with zero external dependencies", and line 209, "Zero external dependencies (Ruby stdlib only)".
2. Line 140, "All Makefile targets include helpful status messages and error handling".
3. Lines 150-154: the "Files monitored for changes" list.
4. Lines 184-205: the "Project structure" tree.

## Evidence

1. Gemfile:7-9 requires the gems cssminify2, json and terser, plus webrick (dev). terser runs through ExecJS, which needs an external JavaScript runtime: `bundle exec ruby -e 'require "execjs"; puts ExecJS.runtime.name'` -> `Bun.sh` here. Pages also loads Tailwind from cdn.tailwindcss.com (_head.html.erb:6). `rg -i 'node|javascript runtime|execjs' README.md Makefile` -> none: the JS-runtime prerequisite is undocumented.
2. Makefile:116-122 swallows failures (see the make test/check/build finding).
3. README:152-154 lists `scripts/*.rb` and "`Makefile`, `README.md`, `Gemfile`". file_watcher.rb:113-122 watches only parse_formulas.rb, build_site.rb and Makefile.
4. README:200-201: `make.rb # Main build script` and `parser.rb # Formula parser`. scripts/parser.rb does not exist. The parser is parse_formulas.rb, and the builder is build_site.rb, absent from the tree along with sync_formulae.rb, asset_processor.rb, time_formatter.rb, file_watcher.rb and serve.rb. `Formula/ └── *.rb` hides the Formula/<letter>/ layout that every formula uses.

## Impact

A contributor who reads "stdlib only" and runs `make build` on a machine without Node or Bun gets an ExecJS::RuntimeUnavailable error that no doc explains. The tree points them at files that do not exist and away from the scripts that matter. The watch list promises that README and Gemfile edits trigger a rebuild, which they do not.

## Fix

- Replace both "zero external dependencies" claims with the real prerequisites: Ruby (see .ruby-version), Bundler, the gems in Gemfile, and a JavaScript runtime for terser (Node.js or Bun).
- Delete line 140's claim, or keep it only after the Makefile finding is fixed.
- Make the watch list match file_watcher.rb: Formula/**/*.rb, theme/**/*, scripts/parse_formulas.rb, scripts/build_site.rb, Makefile.
- Regenerate the scripts/ tree from `ls scripts` with one accurate line each, and show Formula/<letter>/<name>.rb.

## Resolution
README: real prerequisites replace both zero-dependency claims; watch list matches file_watcher.rb; scripts/ tree regenerated; Formula/<letter>/<name>.rb; make.rb section removed; sync behaviour (latest, per-repo failures) and make targets updated.
title: README contradicts the build: "zero external dependencies", wrong watch list and project tree

body:
## Problem

TimeFormatter#format_relative_time, its private helpers calculate_time_difference, format_time_by_category and format_time_unit, and the six SECONDS_PER_* constants have no caller. The only reference outside the module is SiteBuilder::PartialContext#format_relative_time, a forwarder that no template calls. The format_datetime comment says why: relative time "freezes into stale HTML on a static site".

## Evidence

`rg 'format_relative_time|calculate_time_difference|format_time_by_category|format_time_unit|SECONDS_PER_'` outside time_formatter.rb and docs/ finds only build_site.rb:35-36:
```ruby
    def format_relative_time(timestamp)
      @builder.format_relative_time(timestamp)
```
`rg -c format_relative_time theme` -> no matches. The templates use format_date (_footer, _formula_card) and format_datetime (_footer, _formula_card). No template reaches build_site.rb:35.

## Impact

About 45 lines of untested code, including a bare `rescue` that returns "", kept compiling and maintained for nothing. SECONDS_PER_MONTH = 28 days is also inaccurate, so the code would be wrong if anyone wired it back in.

## Fix

Delete format_relative_time, calculate_time_difference, format_time_by_category, format_time_unit and the SECONDS_PER_* constants from time_formatter.rb, and the forwarder at build_site.rb:35-37. format_date and format_datetime stay.

## Resolution
format_relative_time, its helpers and SECONDS_PER_* constants deleted, plus the PartialContext forwarder.
title: format_relative_time and its helpers are dead code

body:
## Problem

Two pieces of repetition carry no information:
- Seven Makefile targets (build, serve, parse, setup, install, update, outdated) each re-derive RUBY_ABI_VERSION and prepend `~/.local/share/gem/ruby/<abi>/bin` to PATH, and each wraps its command in an `if [ -f Gemfile ]` branch with a no-Gemfile fallback. The Gemfile is committed, so that fallback branch never runs.
- file_watcher.rb's all_watched_files unions theme_files (`theme/**/*`) with template_files, style_and_script_files and asset_files. All three are subsets of theme_files, and `.uniq` removes the duplicates on every 1-second poll.

## Evidence

Makefile:35-36, 54-55, 64-65, 93-94, 131-132, 144-145 and 164-165 all contain `RUBY_ABI_VERSION=$$($(RUBY) -e 'puts "#{RUBY_VERSION.split(".")[0]}.#{RUBY_VERSION.split(".")[1]}.0"'); export PATH="$$HOME/.local/share/gem/ruby/$$RUBY_ABI_VERSION/bin:$$PATH"`.
Makefile:34, 53, 63, 91, 125, 141 and 162 each guard with `@if [ -f Gemfile ]`.
file_watcher.rb:89-111: theme_files globs `../theme/**/*`. template_files globs `theme/*.erb`, `theme/_*.erb`, `theme/*.html.erb` and `theme/_*.html.erb`; style_and_script_files globs `theme/*.css` and `theme/*.js`; asset_files globs `theme/assets/**/*`.

## Impact

About 40 lines of Makefile and 20 lines of watcher are noise: every change to how Ruby is invoked has to be made seven times, and the untested no-Gemfile branches drift. The watcher runs eight redundant globs per second.

## Fix

- Makefile: delete the RUBY_ABI_VERSION/PATH lines and the `[ -f Gemfile ]` branches; Bundler already resolves its own binstubs. Define `BUNDLE := bundle exec` once and write each recipe as e.g. `$(BUNDLE) $(RUBY) $(SCRIPTS_DIR)/parse_formulas.rb`.
- file_watcher.rb: delete template_files, style_and_script_files and asset_files, and keep theme_files.

## Resolution
RUBY_ABI_VERSION/PATH lines and Gemfile branches removed; BUNDLE := bundle exec. file_watcher.rb keeps only theme_files for theme/.
title: Makefile repeats a PATH hack seven times; watcher globs theme/ five times

body:
## Problem

The two failure policies point in opposite directions:
- Per release (build_metas), any error is warned and the release dropped. When the dropped release is the newest one, the next release silently becomes `latest`, and the job stays green.
- Per repo (run), the job collects failures and exits 1. In the sync workflow that exit fails the "Generate and validate formulae" step, so no PR is opened for any repo, including the ones that synced fine.

## Evidence

sync_formulae.rb:211-215:
```ruby
    metas = releases.filter_map do |release|
      build_release_meta(source, name, info, release)
    rescue => e
      warn "! #{repo} #{release["tag_name"]}: #{e.message}"
      nil
```
Errors raised there include `asset digest is not sha256` and `mixes archive and raw assets`.

run(): `rescue => e ... failures << repo`, then `exit 1` when failures is non-empty. sync-formulae.yml:39-43 runs this inside the composite action. The PR steps are gated on the diff step, which does not run after a failed step.

## Impact

The newest release of a tool can be skipped silently; for example, it ships assets without a digest, or mixes a raw binary with tarballs. The plain formula then stays on the old version while CI is green. Separately, one unreachable or misconfigured repo, a single transient API failure included, stops updates for all five tools until it recovers.

## Fix

- Make a skipped newest release an error for that repo, not a warning: in build_metas, re-raise when the failing release is `releases.first`.
- In run, still write the formulae of repos that succeeded, and report failures without blocking them. Write the failure list to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` and exit 0 when at least one repo synced. Have the workflow open the PR and post the failures as a PR comment, or fail a separate step after the PR is opened.

## Resolution
A failing latest release raises for that repo. run writes successful repos and, with SYNC_FAILURES_FILE set and at least one success, records failures and exits 0; the action sets the file and sync-formulae.yml fails a step after the PR step, writing failures to the job summary. Local runs still exit 1 on any failure.
title: Skipped releases are only warned about, and one failing repo blocks every repo's update

body:
## Problem

The brew-style hook exits 0 when brew is absent, a guard added in c66e9fe. No other hook runs RuboCop, so on a machine without brew a Ruby commit gets no style or lint check. `make lint` (`bundle exec rubocop`) exists and runs the same vendored homebrew-core config, but no hook calls it.

## Evidence

.pre-commit-config.yaml brew-style entry: `sh -c 'if ! command -v brew ...; then echo "brew not found, skipping brew style"; exit 0; fi; exec brew style --fix --reset-cache .'`. The only other Ruby hook is no-core-class-reopen, a single pygrep.
Makefile:200-202: `lint: ... bundle exec rubocop`.
History shows the style surface breaks repeatedly: 056c543 "fix(lint): drop core-class monkey patches that fail brew style (#70)", 99f25c5 "ci: fix test-bot failures ... (#46)", aef7ba9 "fix(formulae): drop the redundant explicit version (#67)", an audit failure.

## Impact

On machines without brew, including this one, RuboCop offenses are first caught by CI's test-bot after a push, which is the round trip that #46 and #70 show. The local hook passes, so the gap goes unnoticed.

## Fix

Fall back to the brew-free RuboCop run instead of skipping:

```yaml
entry: sh -c 'if command -v brew >/dev/null 2>&1; then exec brew style --fix --reset-cache .; else exec bundle exec rubocop -A; fi'
```

Update the hook comment accordingly. CI still runs the full `brew test-bot --only-tap-syntax` with the brew-only audit cops.

## Resolution
brew-style hook falls back to `bundle exec rubocop -A` when brew is absent; comment updated. prek run --all-files passes locally through the fallback.
title: Without brew, no commit hook lints Ruby, despite recurring brew-style breakage

body:
## Problem

make.rb reimplements build/serve/parse/clean, which the Makefile already provides. Four `ruby-*` "Legacy" targets exist only to call it, and the README documents it as an alternative. Its copies have drifted from the Makefile:
- build runs `system("ruby", ...)` with no `bundle exec`, so `require "terser"` only works when the gems sit in the default gem path.
- clean removes `docs/_templates`, which nothing generates, and misses `docs/assets`, which build does generate.

## Evidence

make.rb:45 and 48: `success = system("ruby", script_path("parse_formulas.rb"))` and `system("ruby", script_path("build_site.rb"))`, without bundler.
Reproduced: `GEM_HOME=<empty> GEM_PATH=<empty> ruby -e 'require "terser"'` -> `LoadError: cannot load such file -- terser`. CI's `make setup` installs into `vendor/bundle` (Makefile:95), which is that case.
make.rb:79: `docs_path("_templates")`. `rg _templates` finds no other reference, and docs/_templates does not exist.
Callers: Makefile:74 (clean), Makefile:260-270 (ruby-build/serve/clean/parse "Legacy" targets), README.md:159-163.

## Impact

Two build entry points with different behavior: `ruby scripts/make.rb build` fails with LoadError where `make build` works, and its clean leaves generated fonts behind. Every change to a build step has to be made twice, and the copies already disagree.

## Fix

Delete scripts/make.rb and the four `ruby-*` targets. Make `clean` a plain recipe:

```make
clean: ## Clean all generated files
	rm -rf $(DOCS_DIR)/index.html $(DOCS_DIR)/formulae.html $(DOCS_DIR)/formula \
	       $(DOCS_DIR)/_data/formulae.json $(DOCS_DIR)/style.css $(DOCS_DIR)/main.js
	find $(DOCS_DIR)/assets -type f ! -name .gitkeep -delete
```

Remove the "Using Ruby Scripts (Alternative)" README section and the make.rb line in the `test` target.

## Resolution
scripts/make.rb deleted with the ruby-* targets; clean is a plain rm/find recipe; README section and test line removed.
title: scripts/make.rb duplicates the Makefile, and its build breaks without Bundler

## Problem

DevServer#initialize sets two instance variables to the same path. Only @site_dir is ever read; @docs_dir is dead.

## Evidence

serve.rb:22: `@site_dir = File.expand_path("../docs", __dir__)`
serve.rb:23: `@docs_dir = File.expand_path("../docs", __dir__)`
`rg -n '@docs_dir|@site_dir' scripts` -> @docs_dir appears only at line 23. @site_dir is read at lines 32 and 52. FileWatcher, the module DevServer includes, does not reference @docs_dir either.

## Impact

A reader has to work out whether the two "docs" paths are meant to differ. They do not, and one is never used.

## Fix

Delete serve.rb:23.

@docs_dir assignment removed from serve.rb.
title: DevServer assigns @docs_dir and never reads it

body:
## Problem

Three files disagree on the Ruby version:
- Gemfile declares `ruby ">= 3.0.0"`.
- .rubocop.yml sets `TargetRubyVersion: "3.0"`, overriding the vendored homebrew-core value of 4.0.
- .ruby-version pins 4.0.7, and CI uses it via setup-ruby.

asset_processor.rb and parse_formulas.rb call `Pathname.new` without `require "pathname"`. That works only because Pathname is a core constant in Ruby 4.0, or because bundler happens to load it.

## Evidence

Gemfile:5: `ruby ">= 3.0.0"`. .rubocop.yml:22: `TargetRubyVersion: "3.0"`. .ruby-version: `4.0.7`.
asset_processor.rb:70 and parse_formulas.rb:90: `Pathname.new(...)`. Neither file requires pathname: asset_processor.rb requires fileutils/terser/cssminify2, and parse_formulas.rb requires json/fileutils/date.
On 4.0.7: `ruby --disable-gems -e 'p defined?(Pathname)'` -> "constant" (core). Nothing tests 3.x.

## Impact

The supported range is a claim nothing exercises. Plain `ruby scripts/parse_formulas.rb` on Ruby 3.x, which the Makefile's no-Gemfile branch and make.rb both do, would fail with `NameError: uninitialized constant Pathname`. RuboCop at target 3.0 also cannot suggest 4.0 idioms.

## Fix

Declare what is actually run and tested: `ruby ">= 4.0"` in the Gemfile, and remove the `TargetRubyVersion: "3.0"` override so the vendored 4.0 applies. Keep a 3.x floor only if you also add `require "pathname"` to both files and a 3.x CI job.

## Resolution
Gemfile declares ruby ">= 4.0"; the TargetRubyVersion 3.0 override was removed from .rubocop.yml so the vendored 4.0 applies (linting-config edit made under the user's "apply all"). RuboCop 1.91.0 reports no offenses.
title: Declared Ruby floor 3.0 is untested; scripts rely on Ruby 4 core Pathname

body:
## Problem

tap-test runs `brew tap-new ivuorinen/homebrew-tap --no-git`, which creates a new, empty tap rather than testing this one. It then runs `brew audit --strict Formula/*.rb`, but every formula lives one level down in Formula/<letter>/, so the glob matches nothing. Both commands' failures are swallowed by `|| true` and `|| echo`.

## Evidence

Makefile:193: `@brew tap-new ivuorinen/homebrew-tap --no-git 2>/dev/null || true`
Makefile:194: `@brew audit --strict $(FORMULA_DIR)/*.rb || echo "⚠️  Some formulae may have audit issues"`

`ls Formula/*.rb` -> "cannot access 'Formula/*.rb': No such file or directory". The inventory shows formulae only at Formula/a/, Formula/g/ and Formula/p/.

## Impact

The target advertised as "Test the tap installation locally" never audits a formula and exits 0. A developer relying on it gets no signal.

## Fix

Audit the tap as CI does, and let failures fail:

```make
tap-test: ## Audit this tap's formulae locally (needs brew)
	brew tap ivuorinen/tap "$$(pwd)"
	brew test-bot --only-tap-syntax --tap=ivuorinen/tap
```

Alternatively `brew audit --strict --tap=ivuorinen/tap`. Drop the `tap-new` line.

## Resolution
tap-test taps the checkout as ivuorinen/tap and runs `brew test-bot --only-tap-syntax --tap=ivuorinen/tap`; tap-new line dropped. Not run locally (no brew).
title: make tap-test audits nothing and always succeeds

body:
## Problem

The tap's name is a literal in five places, with two values:
- "ivuorinen/tap": parse_formulas.rb:121, formula.html.erb:4, formulae.html.erb:4
- "ivuorinen/homebrew-tap": build_site.rb:182, index.html.erb:4

The canonical brew name is ivuorinen/tap; CI runs `brew trust --tap ivuorinen/tap`.

## Evidence

build_site.rb:182: `"tap_name"       => "ivuorinen/homebrew-tap",`
parse_formulas.rb:121: `tap_name:       "ivuorinen/tap",`
index.html.erb:4: `<% safe_tap_name = raw_tap_name.empty? ? 'ivuorinen/homebrew-tap' : raw_tap_name %>`
formulae.html.erb:4 and formula.html.erb:4: `... ? 'ivuorinen/tap' : raw_tap_name %>`

## Impact

Whenever the fallbacks fire, the site shows the non-canonical name in its title and `brew tap` command. That happens with no formulae.json (default_data), or with an empty tap_name. Renaming the tap needs five coordinated edits.

## Fix

Define it once, as `TAP_NAME = "ivuorinen/tap"` in parse_formulas.rb, which writes `tap_name` into the data. Make build_site.rb's default_data use FormulaParser::TAP_NAME, and drop the three template fallbacks: `@data['tap_name']` is always set by one of those two paths.

## Resolution
FormulaParser::TAP_NAME is the single definition; template fallbacks removed. Deviation: build_site.rb's default_data was deleted (missing formulae.json now aborts) instead of importing FormulaParser, keeping stages coupled only through the artifact per arch-profile.
title: Tap name hardcoded in five places with two different values

body:
## Problem

All nine scripts start with `# typed: strict`, a Sorbet sigil that promises every method has a signature and that the file type-checks at strict level. The repo has no Sorbet gem and no `srb tc` step, and no method has a `sig`. brew style does not need the sigil either: in Homebrew's own RuboCop config, Sorbet/StrictSigil and Sorbet/TrueSigil both exclude `Taps/**/*`.

## Evidence

sync_formulae.rb:2 and every other file under scripts/: `# typed: strict`.
`command -v srb` -> not installed. `rg sorbet Gemfile` -> no sorbet gem. No workflow runs srb.
Homebrew/brew Library/.rubocop.yml:395-403: `Sorbet/StrictSigil: Enabled: true, Exclude: - "Taps/**/*" ...`. Lines 408-414 exclude Taps from Sorbet/TrueSigil the same way.

## Impact

A reader, or a tool honouring the sigil, assumes strict static typing guards these scripts. Nothing does. Running Sorbet on them as declared would fail at once on the missing sigs.

## Fix

Remove the `# typed: strict` line from all nine scripts. If static typing is wanted, add sorbet and sorbet-runtime, write sigs, and run `srb tc` in the CI job proposed in the CI finding; only then restore the sigil.

## Resolution
`# typed: strict` removed from all scripts (make.rb deleted).
title: Every script declares `# typed: strict`, but no type checker runs

body:
## Problem

The watcher loop sets `rebuild_pending = true`, rebuilds synchronously on the same thread, then sets it back to false before the next iteration. should_skip_rebuild? therefore always sees false. The flag, its parameter on should_skip_rebuild?, and the reset in the rescue branch guard against a concurrent rebuild that this single-threaded loop cannot produce.

## Evidence

CodeQL 2.26.4, ruby security-and-quality suite: `rb/useless-assignment-to-local` at scripts/file_watcher.rb:21, "This assignment to rebuild_pending is useless, since its value is never read."
file_watcher.rb:19-24:
```ruby
        next if should_skip_rebuild?(current_mtime, last_mtime, rebuild_pending)

        rebuild_pending = true
        handle_file_change(last_mtime)
        last_mtime = perform_rebuild_with_debounce
        rebuild_pending = false
```
The loop runs inside one `Thread.new`, and perform_rebuild_with_debounce blocks it, so the check at line 19 never runs while the flag is true.

## Impact

The code suggests protection against overlapping rebuilds that does not exist and is not needed. A reader changing the loop, for example moving the rebuild to its own thread, will trust a guard that has never executed.

## Fix

Remove the flag:
- delete `rebuild_pending = false` (line 10) and the two assignments at lines 21 and 24;
- delete the reset in the rescue branch (line 29);
- make the check `next if current_mtime <= last_mtime`, and drop should_skip_rebuild?.

## Resolution
rebuild_pending and should_skip_rebuild? removed; check is `next if current_mtime <= last_mtime`.
title: File watcher's rebuild_pending flag is dead logic

body:
## Problem

build_script_files adds parse_formulas.rb and build_site.rb to the watch set, so editing them triggers a rebuild. But DevServer#build_site calls FormulaParser.run and SiteBuilder.build, classes `require_relative`'d once at server start (serve.rb:7-8) and never reloaded. The rebuild runs the pre-edit code. Templates are re-read on every build (build_site.rb:170), so they do pick up changes.

## Evidence

file_watcher.rb:113-117:
```ruby
  def build_script_files
    [
      File.expand_path("../scripts/parse_formulas.rb", __dir__),
      File.expand_path("../scripts/build_site.rb", __dir__),
```
serve.rb:7-8: `require_relative "parse_formulas"`, `require_relative "build_site"`. serve.rb:42-45: `FormulaParser.run` and `SiteBuilder.build`. `rg 'load |reload'` in file_watcher.rb and serve.rb finds nothing.

## Impact

After editing a build script, the watcher prints "📝 Changed: …build_site.rb" and "✅ Rebuild complete", but the output still reflects the old code. That looks like the edit had no effect.

## Fix

Rebuild in a child process so each build loads current code. In serve.rb:

```ruby
  def build_site
    system("ruby", File.join(__dir__, "parse_formulas.rb"), exception: true)
    system("ruby", File.join(__dir__, "build_site.rb"), exception: true)
  end
```

Then drop the two require_relative lines. Alternatively, remove build_script_files from the watch set and document that script edits need a server restart.

## Resolution
DevServer#build_site runs parse_formulas.rb and build_site.rb as child processes; require_relative lines dropped; watch set covers all four build scripts. Verified: touching build_site.rb under a running server triggered a completed rebuild.
title: Dev server watches build scripts but rebuilds with the old code

body:
## Problem

The PreToolUse hook runs `sonar hook claude-pre-tool-use`, documented as "scan files for secrets before agent reads them", only for the `Read` matcher. File contents reach the agent through other tools without passing the scan: Grep, Bash (`cat`, `rg`, `sed`), and MCP readers such as context-mode's ctx_execute_file. Both hooks are also wrapped in `if command -v sonar ...; fi`, so on a machine without sonar they exit 0 with no output. The project looks protected while it is not.

## Evidence

.claude/settings.json:5: `"matcher": "Read"`. Line 9: `"command": "if command -v sonar >/dev/null 2>&1; then sonar hook claude-pre-tool-use; fi"`.
`sonar hook --help` (sonarqube-cli 1.9.0): "claude-pre-tool-use  PreToolUse handler: scan files for secrets before agent reads them".
Observed in this session: nearly every repository file was read via ctx_execute/ctx_execute_file and Bash, which this hook never sees.

## Impact

The secret-scan guarantee covers whatever fraction of reads happen to use Read. An agent that greps or cats a file containing a credential sends it to the model unscanned. On a contributor machine without sonar, nothing is scanned and nothing says so. Today the tree contains no secrets (gitleaks over history; see the security results), so this is defence-in-depth that is narrower than it reads.

## Fix

- Extend the matcher to the other file-reading tools the handler can parse, e.g. `"matcher": "Read|Grep"`, if sonarqube-cli's handler accepts their tool_input. Check `sonar hook claude-pre-tool-use` against a Grep payload first.
- Record the remaining Bash/MCP gap in a comment-equivalent, e.g. a `.claude/README.md` line, so the coverage is not overstated.
- Make the guard visible: `else echo "sonar not installed: prompt/file secret scanning disabled" >&2; fi`. Stderr from a hook that exits 0 is shown without blocking.

## Resolution
Both hooks print to stderr when sonar is missing. Matcher kept at Read: sonar 1.9.0's handler produced no output for Read or Grep payloads against a planted-secret file, so Grep support could not be confirmed (the finding's precondition). The Read-only coverage gap is recorded in .claude/rules/tap.md.
title: Agent secret-scan hook covers only the Read tool and is skipped silently without sonar

body:
## Problem

.PHONY lists 13 targets. The other 18 never produce a file of their name and are not declared phony, so make treats them as file targets: build-production, formula-new, info, lint-fix, lint-update-config, outdated, ruby-build, ruby-clean, ruby-parse, ruby-serve, serve-3000, serve-8080, serve-all, tap-install, tap-test, update-bundler, version, watch.

## Evidence

Makefile:4: `.PHONY: help build serve parse clean test install dev setup check lint update sync`
`grep -oE '^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+:' Makefile` lists 31 targets: the 13 phony ones plus the 18 above.

## Impact

A file or directory named after one of them makes the target silently do nothing ("make: 'info' is up to date."). For example, `version`, `info` or `watch` created by a tool or a stray redirect. Make also stats the filesystem for each undeclared target on every run.

## Fix

Declare every recipe-only target, next to its rule or in one list:

```make
.PHONY: help build sync serve parse clean dev setup check test install update \
        update-bundler outdated watch serve-all serve-3000 serve-8080 build-production \
        tap-test tap-install lint lint-fix lint-update-config formula-new info version
```

Drop the ruby-* names if the make.rb finding is applied.

## Resolution
.PHONY lists all 28 remaining targets; help awk pattern now includes digits so serve-3000/8080 are listed.
title: .PHONY omits 18 of the Makefile's 31 targets

body:
## Problem

parse_formula returns nil, which filter_map drops, in two cases:
- the class regex does not match (`return unless class_name`), with no message at all;
- any exception, caught by `rescue => e` and printed as a warning only.

generate_documentation_data then prints "✅ Successfully generated documentation for N formulae" and exits 0. N is simply smaller.

## Evidence

parse_formulas.rb:55-57:
```ruby
    class_name = extract_value(content, :class_name)

    return unless class_name
```
parse_formulas.rb:67-69: `rescue => e`, `warn "⚠️  Error parsing #{file_path}: #{e.message}"`, `nil`.
PATTERNS[:class_name] = `/^class\s+(\w+)\s+<\s+Formula/`. A formula written `class Foo<Formula`, or one inheriting from a Formula subclass, does not match and is dropped without a word.

## Impact

A formula that exists in the tap and installs fine can be missing from the published docs. The Pages deploy is green and the only trace is a warning line in the log, or nothing. Users browsing the site cannot find a formula that is installable.

## Fix

Fail the run instead of dropping entries. In parse_all_formulae, collect failures and abort after the loop:

```ruby
results = formula_files.map { |f| [f, parse_formula(f)] }
missing = results.select { |_, meta| meta.nil? }.map(&:first)
abort "❌ Could not parse: #{missing.join(", ")}" unless missing.empty?
```

Make parse_formula raise, with the path in the message, when class_name is nil, rather than returning nil.

## Resolution
parse_formula raises ParseError on a missing class line; parse_all_formulae collects every failure and aborts with the list. Verified with a planted Formula/z/zz.rb.
title: Unparseable formula silently disappears from the site while the build succeeds

body:
## Problem

The repo ships .claude/settings.json but no agent instructions: no .claude/rules/, and CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md are gitignored. Three conventions that agents in this repo have broken or would break are recorded only in scattered comments:
1. Formula/ is generated. Every formula header says "generated by scripts/sync_formulae.rb; do not edit by hand", and README:63 says to add the repo to formula-sources.json.
2. No Ruby core-class reopening. The .pre-commit-config.yaml comment explains why brew style fails on it (#70).
3. Scripts must not use brew-only helpers (`exclude?`, `blank?`), because they also run under plain ruby. The build_site.rb:103-105 comment covers this.

## Evidence

.gitignore:29 `AGENTS.md`, :32 `CLAUDE.md`. `ls .claude` -> settings.json only.
Formula/*/*.rb line 3: "generated by scripts/sync_formulae.rb; do not edit by hand".
build_site.rb:103-105: "brew's Homebrew/NegateInclude cop rejects `!include?`, and its suggested `exclude?` only exists inside brew's Ruby".

## Impact

An agent asked to "fix a formula" edits the generated file, and the next daily sync reverts the edit. An agent fixing NegateInclude follows the cop's own suggestion, `exclude?`, and breaks plain-ruby runs. Each rule is discoverable only by reading the file it applies to, after the mistake.

## Fix

Add a tracked `.claude/rules/tap.md` (or a committed AGENTS.md), with three imperative lines:
- "Never edit Formula/**; change scripts/sync_formulae.rb or formula-sources.json and run `make sync`."
- "Never reopen Ruby core classes; brew style fails the tap."
- "In scripts/, use stdlib only: no `exclude?`/`blank?`; swap the predicate instead."

## Resolution
Added tracked .claude/rules/tap.md (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md are gitignored) with the Formula/, core-class, stdlib-only and stage-contract rules.
title: Repo conventions an agent must follow live only in code comments; no agent rule file exists
